title: GH#3: Apply reviewed page changes and restore experiment change sets
body:
## Summary

Resolves #3.

Implements reviewed title and SEO metadata change sets with full-value backups, read-back checks and conflict-aware undo. Integrates the apply time and restore action with experiments across WP-CLI, REST and abilities.

## Implementation

- Files: `includes/stats/class-seoproanalytics-change-sets.php`, schema, experiments, CLI, API and abilities; API contract and SEO-loop documentation
- Pattern: existing experiment commands, routes and abilities
- Scope excludes dashboard controls and fields beyond titles and descriptions

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing level: runtime-verified. Final pushed head: `34d093ce1b235dd788b38b9684b1141bed930bbd`.

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes PHP, JS, shell, workflow, PHPCS, PHPStan and build checks. The build retains its existing webpack bundle-size advisories; no dashboard assets or dependencies changed.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` passes on WordPress latest / PHP 8.3 with 10,000 seeded posts: default and all-feature requests load, query plans pass, uninstall removes the new table, and the PHP error log is clean.
- Disposable WordPress 7.1.3 / Yoast SEO 28.7 acceptance checks pass: two-page dry-run writes nothing; apply preserves full old descriptions including quotes and backslashes beyond 190 bytes; kinds 4/10/11 are tagged with the set id; experiment pages, start time and links agree; undo preserves a later manual edit, restores other fields and removes previously absent metadata.
- Final-head REST and abilities checks pass for preview/apply/list/get/undo, linked experiment restoration, unauthenticated refusal and per-page permission checks. WP-CLI apply/undo and explicit-user enforcement were also exercised during development.
- Final-head hook, KSES and concurrency checks pass: later-save hooks invalidating restored fields and slug changes stop the run; acting-user title sanitization is respected; separate database connections cannot overwrite fields during their compare/write lock; stale cached edits are preserved.
- A separate PHP process holds the page row lock and changes its second planned field before releasing it. Apply waits, skips every field of that stale page without its first mutation, preserves the concurrent edit and continues to the next eligible page.
- Set reads restore the caller's demo/live selection; deleting an experiment retains its full change set. The cursor list uses the primary key.

Additional compatibility evidence: WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 smoke passed at `a20fe39`, before the final isolated whole-page lock fix. Its first attempt failed only on a WordPress core WordPress.org secure-connection warning (`wp-includes/update.php:209`); retry passed without changing the test or suppressing warnings.

## Review

Independent source review identified a whole-page lock-wait race; `34d093c` fixes it and the reviewer accepted the repair with no unresolved P0/P1/P2 defect in that repair. The separate-process runtime regression above reproduces the required timing. Branch evidence bundle SHA-256: `65092a2ea38eca239bc78f3baa84432cead347ee798c3ebb55abcc2c9f24ca50`.

## Decisions

- Full backups and write intent are durable before field mutations; short row-lock transactions guard fresh comparisons and normal WordPress writes.
- First apply writes lock and revalidate every planned field of that page. Later edits remain conflict-aware; the operation is deliberately not an all-pages transaction.
- No dashboard controls, new testing infrastructure, other metadata fields or publication are included.

[UNRELEASED]

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

body:
Bumps [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9.
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.
